question: What major physical change causes teenagers to suddenly need a lot more nutrients in their daily diet?

options.D: The stabilization of adult heart rate

explanation: Rapid skeletal and tissue development requires extra energy and nutrients to sustain bodily remodeling. [learn more](BMP118_U3_T5#BMP118_U3_T5_h1)

question: Why do basic nutritional needs increase so much during the teenage years?

options.A: Digestive efficiency drops by half during these specific years
options.B: Hormonal shifts alter metabolism and body composition changes occur
options.C: Physical activity levels always decrease during secondary school
options.D: Teenagers completely stop storing fat reserves in their tissues

explanation: Endocrine changes and the rapid accumulation of bone and muscle mass drive up the baseline need for fuel and building materials. [learn more](BMP118_U3_T5#BMP118_U3_T5_h1)

question: Which food group should make up the largest part of a teenager's daily energy intake?
explanation: Carbohydrates supply the primary source of sustained energy required to fuel daily activities and rapid physical growth. [learn more](BMP118_U3_T5#BMP118_U3_T5_h2)

question: A 15-year-old boy needs extra building blocks for growing muscles and blood volume. Which dietary component should be prioritized alongside complex carbohydrates?
explanation: Proteins supply the essential amino acids needed to build new lean tissue, enzymes, and blood components during growth spurts. [learn more](BMP118_U3_T5#BMP118_U3_T5_h2)

question: Which nutrient is mainly responsible for expanding blood volume and preventing tiredness in teenagers?
explanation: Iron is a core component of hemoglobin, which carries oxygen through the rapidly expanding blood volume of a growing teenager. [learn more](BMP118_U3_T5#BMP118_U3_T5_h3)

question: What is the main role of Vitamin D in adolescent bone health?

options.A: It helps the body absorb calcium effectively from the diet
options.B: It prevents the breakdown of red blood cells in the bloodstream
options.C: It directly converts into muscle tissue during physical exercise
options.D: It acts as the main source of daily energy for skeletal growth

explanation: Vitamin D acts as a regulator that allows dietary calcium to be properly absorbed and deposited into the developing skeleton. [learn more](BMP118_U3_T5#BMP118_U3_T5_h3)

question: What primary factor creates a higher need for iron in adolescent girls compared to boys?

options.A: The expansion of total body fat reserves
options.C: A higher rate of overall bone lengthening
options.D: An accelerated production of skin oils

explanation: Monthly blood loss depletes iron stores, raising the dietary requirement to prevent deficiency anemia in young females. [learn more](BMP118_U3_T5#BMP118_U3_T5_h4)

question: Why do adolescent males typically need more calories and protein than females of the same age?

options.A: Their physical activity levels are strictly mandated by school rules
options.B: They experience menarche at a much earlier chronological age
options.C: They develop a much larger proportion of lean muscle mass and skeletal volume
options.D: Their digestive systems absorb nutrients at a much slower rate overall

explanation: The male growth spurt involves a massive increase in lean tissue and bone mass, driving up absolute energy and protein needs. [learn more](BMP118_U3_T5#BMP118_U3_T5_h4)

question: Which health condition is most commonly caused by low iron intake combined with monthly blood loss in teenage girls?
explanation: When iron intake cannot keep pace with menstrual losses and growth demands, hemoglobin production drops, resulting in anemia. [learn more](BMP118_U3_T5#BMP118_U3_T5_h5)

question: Which of these is NOT a cause of hidden hunger and vitamin shortages in teenagers?

options.A: Relying heavily on highly processed, refined food products
options.B: Eating excessive amounts of fresh garden vegetables
options.C: Consuming energy-dense foods with very low vitamin content
options.D: Skipping balanced meals in favor of cheap convenience snacks

explanation: Fresh vegetables are rich in micronutrients; eating them prevents, rather than contributes to, hidden hunger. [learn more](BMP118_U3_T5#BMP118_U3_T5_h5)

question: What lifestyle change is a major cause of rising teenage obesity rates in cities?

options.A: The complete elimination of sugary beverages from local markets
options.B: A massive rise in the daily consumption of fresh local vegetables
options.C: Higher levels of rigorous manual farm labor among secondary students
options.D: Increased consumption of processed convenience foods and sedentary habits

explanation: Junk food rich in empty calories paired with less physical movement drives excess weight gain in modern teens. [learn more](BMP118_U3_T5#BMP118_U3_T5_h6)

question: Why is teenage obesity a major long-term health concern for midwives?

options.A: It immediately causes severe iron-deficiency anemia in all cases
options.B: It frequently tracks into adulthood and increases chronic disease risk
options.C: It permanently stops all future skeletal growth and bone lengthening
options.D: It prevents teenagers from ever participating in academic studies

explanation: Obese teenagers are likely to remain obese as adults, raising their lifetime risk of diabetes, high blood pressure, and heart disease. [learn more](BMP118_U3_T5#BMP118_U3_T5_h6)

question: When counseling teenagers on nutrition, what type of food sources should midwives primarily promote?

options.A: Strictly packaged fast foods sold in urban supermarkets
options.B: Entirely liquid meal replacements bought at pharmacies
options.C: Affordable, locally available Nigerian food items
options.D: Expensive dietary supplements imported from overseas

explanation: Promoting accessible local foods ensures that sustainable dietary changes can be maintained by families regardless of income. [learn more](BMP118_U3_T5#BMP118_U3_T5_h7)

question: A teenage girl visits the clinic worried about gaining weight during her puberty growth spurt. How should the midwife best respond?

options.A: Advise her to completely cut out all protein sources from her daily meals
options.B: Tell her to avoid drinking any fluids during the afternoon hours
options.C: Explain that healthy weight gain during puberty is normal and necessary for future health
options.D: Recommend an immediate strict crash diet to stop all further physical development

explanation: Reassuring teenagers about normal body changes fosters a positive body image and supports healthy physical development. [learn more](BMP118_U3_T5#BMP118_U3_T5_h7)
